_about: Hand-written from City of Toronto pages, read Nov 17, 2026. 'when' says which projects an item applies to (see checker/roadmap.py). Check the City's pages for changes before relying on this.

sources.name: Small Residential Additions (required documentation and forms)
Municipal Code Chapter 363, s. 363-3.5 (plans and site plan requirements; Schedule D)
When to Call for Inspection of Small Buildings

general: All drawings on standard-size sheets, drawn to scale, fully dimensioned, signed and dated (Ch. 363-3.5C).
Submit everything as single-layer PDFs (version 7 or later), with comments and layers removed.
If a qualified designer drew the plans: their name, BCIN registration number, signature and stamp on the drawings.
Don't put personal information (names, phone numbers) on the drawings: plans can be disclosed under MFIPPA.

drawings.detail: Referenced to a current survey by an Ontario Land Surveyor. Shows lot size and dimensions, setbacks to existing and proposed buildings, existing and finished grades and street elevations, easements and services, setbacks to buildings on the neighbouring lots, and a summary of permitted vs proposed zoning (lot area, floor area, coverage, height).
Every level, fully dimensioned: existing and proposed uses of each room, smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, plumbing fixtures, walls, and the structure above.
Roof structure, slopes, skylights, hips/valleys/peaks and ventilation.
Exterior finishes, roof slopes, window and door sizes and sill heights, overall building height, decks/stairs/guards, and the area of exposed wall and unprotected openings (limiting distance).
Floor, wall and roof assemblies, footings and foundation walls, grade height above the basement floor, floor-to-floor and floor-to-ceiling heights, stairs and guards.
Location and setbacks on the site plan, distance to other buildings, parking spaces and driveway, floor plans, elevations, sections and the concrete slab details.
Footing size, spacing, depth and frost protection; column and beam sizes and spans; stair rise, run and headroom; guard details (openings, climbability).
What is being demolished, how, and the schedule (Ch. 363-3.4).
Submitted as their own PDFs for the HVAC and plumbing permit applications.

forms.item: Application for a Permit to Construct or Demolish
forms.detail: The provincial form (updated version required since Feb 16, 2026). This tool pre-fills part of it.
For the designer (not needed for engineers and architects). Homeowners designing their own house fill it in to claim the exemption.
For a new house or an addition: prescriptive or performance compliance form.
Required wherever private or City trees could be damaged.
For new houses and additions over 100 m²: you then post the City's notice on site.
A deposit that covers damage to the curb, sidewalk, road or boulevard during construction.

forms.item: Assumption of Responsibility for Engineering Content
forms.detail: Only if a professional engineer sealed any drawings.
For renovations to a rental unit (Chapter 662).
Signed by the designer for every new building or addition.

inspections.call: When the formwork is done, before pouring concrete.
When framing is complete, including rough-in plumbing and HVAC.
When wall, floor and shaft separations and fire stopping are done, before interior finishes.
When insulation and vapour barrier are done, before interior finishes.
When water supply, drains, waste and vents are roughed in and ready for testing.
When the rough-in is complete, before insulation.
Ask your inspector (needed before anyone moves in).
When the exterior is complete. This closes the permit: an open permit can cause trouble when you sell.

inspection_notes: Tell your inspector when each stage is ready. Inspections happen within two business days of your request (Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4:30).
Keep the stamped permit drawings on site for every inspection.
Don't cover anything before it passes: covered work has to be opened up again.
